sentences.text: Appearance:
Shri Mayank Mishra - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Madhusudan Yadav - Govt. Advocate for the respond  ORDER

This second application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.385/2024 registered at Police Station, Sanwer District Indore (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 466, 467, 473 and 474 of IPC.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 27.07.2024.
Applicant's first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 22.10.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 42916/2024.
As per the case of prosecution, Ankit Patel submitted a complaint alleging forgery of a Court order produced in appeal for mutation proceedings.
It was alleged that Narendra Jat had purchased the land from Harishankar in violation of the stay order passed by the Court of Civil Judge.
In mutation proceedings , a copy of the order dated 10.03.2008 passed in Appeal No. 44/2005 was filed which is allegedly NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6849 2 MCRC-9724-2025 forged.
After inquiry, P.S. Sanwer registered FIR for offence punishable u / S 420, 466, 467, 473 and 474 of IPC against Narendra Jat and Harishankar Patel.
The relevant record of the appellate proceedings before the SDO Sanwer was seized.
A copy of the order in question was also seized at the instance of Narendra Jat.
However, the original copy of the order could not be recovered.
Narendra Jaat was arrested on 24.07.2024.
He is in custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted on 22.10.2024 pending investigation against absconding against M.S. Khan.

sentences.text: The trial is underway.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant is falsely implicated in the matter.
He has purchased the land from the title holder - Harishankar Patel and paid the amount through account payee cheques to him.
He is a bonafide purchaser.

Learned counsel referring to appeal memo and written submissions made on behalf of applicant - Narendra Jaat in the mutation proceedings contends that the applicant did not refer the order in question in the appeal memo or the written submission.
He has not produced the copy of the order which is alleged to be forged.
The original copy of such order was not recovered at the instance of the applicant.
Learned counsel further contends that the applicant is aged 30 years.
He is an agriculturist by profession and is the sole bread earner of the family.
The prosecution is based on documentary evidence.
There is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6849 3 MCRC-9724-2025 no likelihood of tampering with evidence by the applicant.
Further custodial interrogation of the applicant is not needed.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned counsel contends that the applicant was ultimate beneficiary of the order in question filed before the SDO, Sanwer in mutation appeal proceedings.
Therefore, the complicity of the applicant in forging the order can be inferred.
The order of Civil Court is forged, which shows the gravity of allegations.
Therefore, applicant may not be extended the benefit of bail.

However,
after going through the case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
Heard the arguments, perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application and the case diary.
The case diary and material on record reveals that the applicant is implicated on suspicion of forging the Court order and producing it in mutation appeal proceedings.
The forgery of the order is yet to be substantiated by the examination of hand writing expert.
The original copy of the order could not be recovered during investigation.
The veracity of the prosecution will be determined in evidence at the trial.
The prosecution is based on documentary evidence.
All the relevant documents have been seized.
There is no likelihood of tampering with NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6849 4 MCRC-9724-2025 evidence by the applicant.
As per information, applicant is aged around 30 years.
He is an agriculturist by profession and is sole bread earner of family.
Considering the age and family status of applicant, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.

In absence of any criminal antecedent, considering the socio-economic status of the applicant and the complainant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with evidence or influencing the witnesses by the applicant.
The trial would take time to conclude.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the applicant.

However, it is clarified that the observations,
herein above, are recorded for present application only.

Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforestated facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant - Narendra Jat shall be released on bail in connection with the Crime as stated in para-1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount, as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court for compliance with conditions, as may be imposed by such Court under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C. 1973 / Section 480(3) of BNSS,
2023, to secure presence of the applicant for the trial.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial.

However, in case of breach of any of the preconditions of bail, the Trial Court may NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6849 5 MCRC-9724-2025 consider, on merit, cancellation of bail without any impediment of this order.
The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
C.C. as per rules
